subject: Live checkout: intermittent framing errors causing elevated 5xx/latency (exec escalation)
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha@peakretail.com>

Cc: Tomas Ortega <tomas.ortega@peakretail.com>, Peak Retail Support <support@peakretail.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in 500s and latencies on Live Checkout after SDK v2.4.1

Karthik / Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp spike in 5xx errors and p99 latency on our live checkout at ~07:45 PST this morning. The only recent change on our stack was rolling the Redwood client SDK to v2.4.1 last night. Traffic pattern is normal; the errors are concentrated on the streaming payment-authorize endpoint.

Symptoms:
- 5xx rate jumped from 0.4% to ~8% across 07:45-08:00
- P99 latency for the checkout flow increased from 430ms to 2.2s
- Partial traces show repeated TCP-level reconnects and truncated response frames

We attached a sample of client traces and a small repro that reliably shows the error when we replay real traffic against your staging endpoint (sdk-trace-20280307.gz, repro-minimal.patch).

This is causing cart abandonment on our highest-volume region; our CRO has asked for an immediate update. Please confirm receipt and next steps.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Li
Head of Integrations — Peak Retail

Attachments: sdk-trace-20280307.gz, repro-minimal.patch

Subject: Re: Spike in 500s and latencies on Live Checkout after SDK v2.4.1

Samantha — thanks for the quick heads up and for the traces. We have triaged this as high priority. I reproduced the truncated-frame behavior locally against our ingestion harness and have paged Soojin (protocol team) and Marcus (runtime) to investigate root cause.

Immediate actions we are taking:
- Rollback suggestion: If you can temporarily pin to v2.4.0 that should mitigate; our telemetry shows compatibility regressions introduced in v2.4.1 under multiplexed streams.
- We’ll validate a hotfix for v2.4.2 and share a patch/timestamps within 3 hours.
- Opening a support ticket SUP-4821 and sharing reproducible steps with our eng team.

I’ll coordinate an exec-brief if this does not resolve within the next 2 hours.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Spike in 500s and latencies on Live Checkout after SDK v2.4.1

Folks — initial read: traces show a recurring pattern of partial frame reads where the client-side chunk boundary occurs mid-header; the streaming parser on the server ends up treating the fragment as an invalid header and responds with a 500. Under normal single-frame requests we don't see this; it manifests under high concurrency + multiplexing (exactly what v2.4.1 changed).

Key notes:
- Repro is reliable for us when we enable concurrent streams=8 in the repro script.
- Hypothesis: client-side coalescing change in v2.4.1 altered write() batching. Server parser assumed header alignment per earlier SDK behavior and lacked robust reassembly for header slices.
- Quick mitigation: strengthen server-side header reassembly and add defensive parsing for partial headers.

I'm going to push a small parser guard (safe-reassemble) to a branch and run it against Peak's repro. Marcus, can you run the runtime with extended logging for header assembly?

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Protocol Engineering — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: peakretail-live-logs-20280307.csv
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Mar 2028 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 500s and latencies on Live Checkout after SDK v2.4.1

Running the repro now in a scaled harness (8 parallel streams). Observing the same truncated-frame exception in the runtime logs at about 12-15% of requests in the replay — translated into 500s in the customer traces. Pushing a debug build that logs the exact byte offsets for the header parse.

Temporary mitigation options:
1) Heavier TCP Nagle disable on client to avoid batching small writes (works but intrusive for customers).
2) Server-side conservative reassembly (I have a branch ready, will smoke test in 30m).
3) Hotfix rollback in CDN layer to strip the v2.4.1 client version and route to compat pool (requires infra ops signoff).

Suggest we run the conservative reassembly change as a hotfix first. If it passes smoke tests against Peak repro, we then push it to prod for affected routes and simultaneously prepare a v2.4.2 client patch.

—Marcus
